extra_prompt: You are booking for a licensed pest control company. Ask what pest is involved, where it has been seen, and how long the problem has lasted. Ask whether there are children, pets, or elderly residents, because they affect the treatment plan. Tell the caller not to disturb a nest or spray it themselves. Bee or wasp nests near people, or a stinging risk, are urgent. Treatment depends on inspection, so do not name chemicals or give dosing advice.

kb.q: Are your treatments safe for pets and children?
kb.a: We choose products suited to the pest and the site. We tell you which areas to keep clear and how long to stay out after treatment, so please follow the instructions our technician gives you.

kb.q: How long before I can return after a treatment?
kb.a: Most treatments need you to stay out of treated rooms until the spray has dried, usually a few hours. Our technician gives you exact instructions on site before leaving.

kb.q: How much does an inspection cost?
kb.a: {price_note} A standard pest inspection includes a written report with recommended treatment options. Ask us what is included before you book.

kb.q: Do you offer a guarantee?
kb.a: Yes. {guarantee_note} Ask us what the guarantee covers and how long it lasts before you book.

kb.q: Do you treat termites?
kb.a: Yes. We offer termite inspections and treatments, including barrier and bait options. We provide a termite report that buyers and sellers can use.

kb.q: I found a termite mound or live termites. What should I do?
kb.a: Do not disturb them or try to treat yourself. Keep the area as it is, and book a termite inspection as soon as possible so we can assess the damage.

kb.q: Do you remove rats and mice?
kb.a: Yes. We inspect, seal entry points, set bait stations or traps, and check for repeat activity over the following weeks. Keep food in sealed containers while we work.

kb.q: Can you remove a wasp or bee nest?
kb.a: Yes. We remove wasp nests and relocate or remove honey bee swarms where we can. Tell us at booking if anyone in the house has a known sting allergy so we can prioritise the visit.

kb.q: Do you handle bed bugs?
kb.a: Yes. Bed bug treatment usually needs more than one visit, and we advise on preparing bedding, furniture and clothing. Follow our preparation guide before the first visit.

kb.q: Do you treat cockroaches?
kb.a: Yes. We treat cockroaches with gel baits and targeted sprays. We also advise on food storage and cleaning to help prevent a return.

kb.q: How often should I have pest control?
kb.a: Many homes and businesses benefit from a preventive service every three to six months. The right interval depends on the pest pressure at your property, and we will recommend a plan after the inspection.

kb.q: Are ants a serious problem?
kb.a: Ants are usually a nuisance rather than a risk, but some species nest in walls. An inspection finds the nest so we can treat it properly.

kb.q: Do you do spider treatments?
kb.a: Yes. We treat spider harbourage areas inside and outside the home. We can also advise on reducing the food and shelter spiders use around the property.

kb.q: Do you treat outdoor areas?
kb.a: Yes. We treat perimeters, eaves, gardens and bins where pests enter or breed. Outdoor treatments are often combined with an interior visit.

kb.q: Will I need to prepare the property?
kb.a: Usually only light preparation is needed: clear benchtops and food storage, and let the technician know where children and pets are. Your technician will tell you if anything else is needed.

kb.q: Are your technicians licensed?
kb.a: Our technicians hold [licence type and number] for pest control. Ask us for that number before we attend, and we will show you the products we use on arrival.

kb.q: Do you do commercial pest control?
kb.a: Yes. We service restaurants, offices, warehouses and strata buildings with scheduled visits. We keep a logbook that can be provided for audits.

kb.q: What is a pre-purchase pest inspection?
kb.a: It is a visual inspection of the property for termites, borers and other pests, with a written report. It helps you decide before you buy, but it does not replace a full building inspection.

kb.q: Can you stop birds nesting in my roof or eaves?
kb.a: Yes. We install bird exclusion netting and mesh and seal entry points. We use humane exclusion methods and check the rules that apply to native birds before any work starts.

kb.q: Can you control mosquitoes around the home?
kb.a: We can treat breeding areas and apply a targeted spray. Removing standing water in gutters, pot plates and pet bowls is the most effective step you can take between visits.

kb.q: Do you control flies?
kb.a: Yes. We look for the source, such as bins, drains or animal waste, and treat it with a fly control program. Clearing the source is usually the quickest way to reduce flies.

kb.q: Do you treat pests in apartments or units?
kb.a: Yes. We coordinate with the strata or building manager and treat common areas and adjoining units where needed. Written notice is given to residents before any treatment.

kb.q: How can I tell if I have a rodent problem?
kb.a: Look for droppings, gnaw marks, scratching in the ceiling or walls, and a musky smell. A visit confirms it and finds the entry points.

kb.q: Do you treat moisture and drainage pests?
kb.a: Yes. Pests such as silverfish and cockroaches often follow damp areas. We check drainage, ventilation and moisture sources along with the treatment.
